solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sort originally from region around here? Not he

definitions.text: Sort originally from region around here? Not he

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange, so all the gathered letters are shuffled
originally asks for the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: its first letter
taken as written

indicators.note: Not says the following letters are excluded from the word before

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A local's sniffy verdict on some newcomer: he is not originally from round here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not he' strips HE from here, leaving RE, which region goes around; 'originally' adds F, and 'Sort' rearranges the whole pool. The whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreigner is someone who comes from another country or, colloquially, from outside the local area.

clue.text: Obsessive after glimpse of flashing lighthouse in the past

indicators.note: a glimpse is only a brief partial view, so just the first letter of the following word is seen

parts.note: the first letter of flashing
anal is informal for fussily obsessive about detail

explanation.surface: A fixated person watching for the flash of an old lighthouse.
explanation.walkthrough: After places the obsessive word behind the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fanal is an archaic word for a beacon or lighthouse, hence the marker of an obsolete term.

clue.text: Iowan mob condemned witch

indicators.note: something condemned is wrecked or ruined, so the preceding letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: the letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lynch mob in Iowa passes sentence on a woman accused of witchcraft.
explanation.walkthrough: Obi (or obeah) is a form of West Indian sorcery, so an obi-woman practises it.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi-woman is a female practitioner of obeah sorcery, which makes her a sorceress.

clue.text: Vape offering formality about end of fag?

indicators.note: about suggests turning about, so the word for formality is read from its far end

parts.note: ice can mean chilly formality or reserve of manner

indicators.note: end of picks out only the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the last letter of fag

explanation.surface: A vape shop offering something about the end of the cigarette habit.
explanation.walkthrough: A fag is British slang for a cigarette; the question mark admits that the definition is the device, not the act.
explanation.definitionFit: An e-cig, electronic cigarette, is the device people call a vape, used instead of smoking tobacco.

clue.text: I tempt back current oil producer

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word for tempt is read right to left

parts.note: taken as written
a pull is an attraction, so to pull is to lure or tempt
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone tries to tempt us back to the current price of oil.
explanation.walkthrough: The illupi is an Indian tree whose seeds yield a fat used as oil.
explanation.definitionFit: The illupi, or mahua, is a tropical tree whose seeds yield a valuable cooking and lamp fat.

clue.text: I return our awful food

indicators.note: something awful is in a dreadful state, so the preceding letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: A diner sending back an awful meal at a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an old word borrowed from French.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourriture is an archaic word for nourishment, sustenance or provisions eaten to live.

clue.text: Spectre's blown up James with no justice

indicators.note: blown means scattered as if by wind, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: with no says the following letter is taken away from the name

parts.note: taken as written
J is the standard abbreviation for justice, as in a judge's title

explanation.surface: A ghost story in which some James is blown up, with justice never done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no justice' drops J from James, leaving AMES. 'blown up' reads as one phrase meaning exploded, but only 'blown' signals the rearrangement and up is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Empusa was a shape-shifting female demon or hobgoblin sent by Hecate, a kind of phantom.

clue.text: State control set-up is constrained by small amount of money

indicators.note: something constrained is held in, so the first part sits inside the coin word

parts.note: a dime is a US ten-cent coin
a rig is an apparatus or arrangement
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political claim that state control is held back by a lack of funds.
explanation.walkthrough: D(RIG IS)ME. A dime is a US ten-cent coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirigisme is the economic doctrine of central government planning and direction of the economy.

clue.text: Glacial mass lecturer besieged by environmentalists

indicators.note: a besieged place is surrounded, so the lecturer letter is placed inside the group

parts.note: FoE is Friends of the Earth, an environmental group
L is the abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: A glaciology lecturer surrounded by green protesters.
explanation.walkthrough: F(L)OE.
explanation.definitionFit: A floe is a sheet of floating ice, a large mass detached from a glacier or ice field.

clue.text: Chevrotain going round grass mound rolling

indicators.note: going round means turning to face back, so the grass word reads backwards

parts.note: a reed is a tall waterside grass

indicators.note: a thing rolling over turns end to end, so the mound word is read backwards

parts.note: a tel is an archaeological mound in the Middle East

explanation.surface: A small deer trotting round some grass and rolling down a hillock.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate reversal signals each turn one piece; tel is a word from Middle Eastern archaeology.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevrotain, or mouse deer, is a tiny deer-like ruminant, sometimes called a deerlet.

clue.text: Shopping bag overturned set of scales

indicators.note: something overturned ends up upside down, so the bag word is read backwards

parts.note: a caba, or cabas, is a shopping basket or reticule

explanation.surface: A shopping bag knocked over onto a pair of scales.
explanation.definitionFit: An abac is a nomogram, a chart with graduated scales for reading off calculations.

clue.text: Search endlessly on Bing — it's what I do

indicators.note: endlessly says the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to comb is to search thoroughly
bing is a dialect word for a heap or pile, listed in Chambers

explanation.surface: Someone searching on Bing, the Microsoft search engine, is told to keep at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims COMB. 'Bing' looks like the search engine, matching 'Search', but it is an old word for a heap. 'I' is the setter, who compiles crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword setter is called a compiler, so compiling is what the setter speaking in the clue does.

clue.text: Nearly no good, nearly type nothing

indicators.note: no says the following letter is left out

parts.note: nigh means nearly, as in nigh on

indicators.note: nearly says the word is not quite complete, so its last letter goes

parts.note: ilk means type or kind, as in of that ilk

explanation.surface: A grumble that some work is nearly useless, nearly worthless as a type.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Nearly' is a synonym, not an instruction: it gives NIGH, which then has 'no good' applied. The second 'nearly' trims ILK.
explanation.definitionFit: Nihil is the Latin word for nothing, used in English for a thing of no value.

clue.text: Possibly until I used … it's this?

definitions.text: Possibly until I used … it's this?

indicators.note: possibly hints at one possible arrangement among many of the letters

parts.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: Something lay idle until somebody used it, so what was it before?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: until I used it, a thing was not in use.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not put to use before I employed it was idle, never yet exploited.

clue.text: Beginning to undo rope tangled round hard wooden block

indicators.note: Beginning to asks for the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: its first letter

indicators.note: round says the rearranged rope goes round the letter for hard
tangled means twisted into a knot, so the letters of rope are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
H is the standard abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A sailor starts to undo a rope tangled round a hard wooden block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangled' rearranges rope to PROE, which goes 'round' H, after the U from 'Beginning to undo'.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship an uphroe is a long wooden block with holes, used to adjust the lines of an awning.

clue.text: Shakespeare's region cut crop that's ripe

indicators.note: cut says the word is shortened, here by its final letter

parts.note: to crop is to clip, as with hair
mature means ripe, ready to eat

explanation.surface: A farmer cuts a crop that has ripened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' and 'crop' both look like the harvest; here crop is the synonym and cut the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Climature is a word used once by Shakespeare in Hamlet for a region or clime, as Chambers records.

clue.text: Boundless charity event, one that remains more rowdy

indicators.note: boundless means without its bounds, so the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: a fun run is a sponsored race held to raise money for charity
a lier is one who lies, that is, remains in place

explanation.surface: A charity event without limits, where only one participant stays on, gets out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boundless' strips the outer letters of FUN RUN. 'one that remains' looks like a survivor; it is one that lies, stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrulier is the comparative of unruly, meaning more disorderly and harder to control.

clue.text: Slump? Money's short

indicators.note: falling short means the last letter of the money word is missing

parts.note: lolly is British slang for cash

explanation.surface: An economic slump explained by a shortage of money.
explanation.walkthrough: Slump is a verb here, to slouch, not a downturn.
explanation.definitionFit: To loll is to lounge or sprawl lazily, just as one slumps in a chair.

clue.text: Royal surrendering rule like in Richard III?

indicators.note: surrendering means giving up, so the rule abbreviation is given away

parts.note: regal means royal
R is the abbreviation for rule; it is the letter given up

explanation.surface: A king giving up his rule, as Richard III does in the play.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the abbreviation for rule. Richard III marks the word as Shakespeare's, used in that play.
explanation.definitionFit: Egal is an old word for equal, meaning just alike or the same, used by Shakespeare in Titus and Richard III.

clue.text: Liberal close to entering a ballot at pleasure

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so the first pieces are put within the ballot

parts.note: taken as written
a ballot is a vote
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
on can mean next to or near, as in a house on the river

explanation.surface: A Liberal candidate edging closer to winning a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: A VO(L ON)TE. Close to is not a last-letter signal here; it means near.
explanation.definitionFit: A volonté is a French phrase used in music meaning freely, as the performer wishes.

clue.text: Idiot once more dropping nuclear weapon

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it go, so the nuclear abbreviation is lost

parts.note: again means once more
N is the abbreviation for nuclear; it is the letter dropped

explanation.surface: A fool, yet again, letting go of a nuclear weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the abbreviation for nuclear.
explanation.definitionFit: An assagai, or assegai, is a slender throwing spear of southern Africa, a hunting and war weapon.

clue.text: One indigenous species around SA I lead

indicators.note: around says the species word goes on either side of the next two pieces

parts.note: Roman numeral one
an indigenous species is native
SA is sex appeal, which is also called it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A conservation officer leading a project on a native species in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: SA looks like South Africa; here it is sex appeal, which old slang calls it.
explanation.definitionFit: To take the initiative is to take the lead, acting first before others do.

clue.text: Sweden accepted aliens, backing centre for those helping the distressed

parts.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
A is an abbreviation for accepted, as in commerce on bills

indicators.note: backing centre says the middle letters of the word are turned round

parts.note: Martians are aliens from Mars

explanation.surface: Sweden is praised for taking in refugees, backing a centre for the distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing centre' reverses the two middle letters of MARTIANS. The Samaritans are a British charity offering a phone line to people in despair.
explanation.definitionFit: The Samaritans are volunteers who listen to people in emotional distress or at risk of suicide.

clue.text: Note number plate on A road

parts.note: reg is short for a car's registration number
taken as written
Rd is the address abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Jotting down a car's number plate seen on an A road.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an A road is a main road.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to observe or pay attention to it, which is what regard means as a verb.

clue.text: US football star headed ball, support lacking at the back

indicators.note: headed here means beheaded, so the first letter of the ball word goes
the support word is missing its last letter

parts.note: the word without its head
a prop is a support; its last letter then goes

explanation.surface: An American footballer heading the ball with no backing from teammates.
explanation.walkthrough: Headed tempts as a football action; it means beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-pro is a player picked for the season's all-star team in American professional football.

clue.text: Starts to shout noisily as pairs appear in this?

definitions.text: Starts to shout noisily as pairs appear in this?

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so the first letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Players yelling loudly whenever matching cards turn up in a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the game: players shout when two matching cards appear.
explanation.definitionFit: Snap is a children's card game where players call out when two matching cards are turned up.

clue.text: Tree workmate cut down by morning

parts.note: a.m. stands for the morning hours

indicators.note: knocked down means turned over, so the workmate word is read backwards
something cut is shortened, so the turned word loses its last letter

parts.note: a pal is a friend or mate

explanation.surface: A colleague hewing a tree in the early morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The mate is turned and shortened to LA, placed by AM.
explanation.definitionFit: The amla, or emblic, is an Indian tree whose sour fruit is used in medicine and cooking.

clue.text: Quizzer from Scotland to search after answer

indicators.note: after places the Scots search word behind the single letter, so the clue order is swapped

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
a Scots form meaning to scour or search

explanation.surface: A quizmaster from Scotland searching for the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scots word goes after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who asks questions, a questioner, is a quizzer by another name.

clue.text: What'll encourage a woman to follow international rugby league?

parts.note: at and to both mark place, as in at home and to hand
to tag along is to follow
I is the abbreviation for international
RL is the usual abbreviation for rugby league

explanation.surface: Should a woman be encouraged to take up following international rugby league?
explanation.walkthrough: A woman reads as part of the wordplay; it belongs to the definition, and the rest builds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Attagirl is an exclamation of praise or encouragement addressed to a woman or girl.

clue.text: Struggle wasting energy and time in office

indicators.note: wasting means using up and losing, so these letters are thrown away

parts.note: the offices is an old euphemism for the lavatory, so an office is a toilet

explanation.surface: A worker struggles with wasted energy and time in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting' removes E and T. 'office' looks like a workplace to match the struggle, but it is a euphemism for the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: To toil is to labour hard or struggle with something difficult.

clue.text: Almost puncture close to kerb. Spare tyre?

indicators.note: almost means not quite, so the last letter of the puncture word goes

parts.note: a flat is a punctured tyre

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of kerb

explanation.surface: A motorist nearly gets a puncture by the kerb and reaches for the spare tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: A spare tyre is jokey slang for a roll of fat round the waist; the question mark flags it.
explanation.definitionFit: Flab is loose body fat, and a spare tyre is the roll of it round someone's middle.

clue.text: Pigeons generally regarded as safe besetting man in East London

indicators.note: to beset is to surround on all sides, so the safety initials enclose the man

parts.note: GRAS is the US food-safety label generally recognized as safe
ou is South African slang for a man, and East London is a South African city

explanation.surface: Pigeons in the East End being declared harmless.
explanation.walkthrough: East London is not the Cockney East End but the South African port, where an ou is a bloke.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouras are large crowned pigeons of New Guinea, the genus Goura.

clue.text: Political principle, Keir's first added to road map?

parts.note: a road map is a plan of action

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the leader's name

parts.note: the first letter of Keir, as in Keir Starmer

explanation.surface: Keir Starmer's first policy point added to Labour's road map.
explanation.walkthrough: Keir Starmer is the Labour leader; road map is a plan, not a map.
explanation.definitionFit: A plank is one item in a party's political platform, a single policy commitment.

clue.text: Staff on plane triumphed after first class run

indicators.note: after sends the word for triumphed to the end, behind the class and run pieces

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
crew is a past tense of crow, to exult in triumph

explanation.surface: Flight staff celebrating after a first-class run.
explanation.walkthrough: Crew is the old past tense of crow, still used in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The aircrew are the people who fly and serve on an aircraft.

clue.text: Fixed stake in agrarian terrain

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the phrase that follows, spanning its two words

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A farmer's fixed share in a piece of farmland.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ante is a set stake each player puts in before the deal.

clue.text: Bojo branded an abject rogue, he does occasional work around the House

definitions.text: he does occasional work around the House

indicators.note: rogue means behaving wildly, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written; Bojo is the nickname of the former prime minister Boris Johnson

indicators.note: to abject is an old verb meaning to cast out, so the letters of an are thrown out

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson is branded an abject rogue by a man who works around the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abject' looks like an adjective in 'an abject rogue', but it is the old verb to cast out, removing AN from branded before 'rogue' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd-jobber does odd jobs, casual tasks such as repairs around a house.
